email.subject: MV VALDA CREST - Rotterdam line-up: berth occupied
email.body:
Dear Operations,

MV VALDA CREST - Rotterdam, Rijnmond Energy Coal Terminal

The coal berth is occupied. The vessel ahead is expected to complete discharge late on 26 Jan. VALDA CREST is next in line, berthing about 27 Jan 0600 UTC, subject to the vessel ahead completing as planned.

We will advise at once if the line-up changes. Please keep us informed of the vessel's ETA.

Best regards,
Operations desk
Maasport Agencies, Rotterdam

result.result: The agent's berthing time is provisional — "about 27 Jan 0600 UTC, subject to the vessel ahead completing as planned" — not a firm commitment, so cutting speed now is a judgment call rather than a certainty. The speed advice from the voyage optimisation service (simulated figures for this demo) is 8.3 knots to arrive at the Rotterdam pilot station on 27 Jan 04:00 UTC, two hours before the provisional berth, saving an estimated 31 hours at anchor and about 38.1 tonnes of VLSFO against the 12.4 kn base; the speed plan checks out as consistent. Heavy weather is forecast on the route from 22 Jan evening to 24 Jan (wind up to Beaufort 8 astern, seas to 6.1 m), so the Master's safety judgement comes first. The operator should decide whether to order the reduced speed. If yes: (a) a speed instruction to the Master at 8.3 kn with arrival 27 Jan 04:00 UTC, subject to his safety judgement in the weather ahead; (b) the ETA notice the CP says is due — the ETA has moved 31 hours against a 12-hour limit — to the agent and receiver with the new ETA 27 Jan 04:00 UTC; and (c) a voyage management system port-call ETA entry for Rotterdam at 27 Jan 04:00 UTC. Nothing should be sent until the operator answers.

The ETA at Rotterdam pilot station has moved to 27 Jan 04:00 UTC, which is 31 hours beyond the 12-hour charterparty limit. The coal berth at Rotterdam is occupied, and berthing is now expected about 27 Jan 0600 UTC.

We will keep you updated as the situation develops.

Best regards,
Operations

Operations
